verification_report.summary: The lemma, theorem, and corollary are correct under the explicitly accepted compact-curve, ideal-envelope, and source-metric inputs. Countable atomic removal is valid for the finite curvature measure; the distributional difference q_D-w_D has a globally bounded quasi-psh representative; the residual curvature is nonpolar even if the potentials have additional polar points; and the endpoint D_u(Y)=A has zero non-pluripolar mass, establishing surjectivity onto the positive-mass envelopes. In the finite-support maximum, the bounded local remainder identifies the minimum Lelong profile and yields the required mass. The verified SGPT estimates give C_1=48 and hence the sharp stated constants 1/96 and 1/2 with the full total-variation normalization. Finite-tail approximation handles countable supports without any infinite-support maximum identification. The atomic mass-capped locus is complete in total variation, finite rational profiles approximate from below even at the boundary, and the family {a delta_p} is uniformly d_S-separated, proving failure of total boundedness. No Popovici, capacity-convergence, or general Hermitian metric input is used.
